dramatic.state_in: Greg can begin alteration but cannot cleanly halt it while maintaining draw.
dramatic.required_result: Reframe stopping as ending deliberate feed and allowing the alteration to settle.
dramatic.state_out: The alteration diminishes under a better instruction, followed by a small wrist twitch.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns instruction framing; Greg owns sensory distinctions.

performance.behavior: Hessa changes STOP to ENOUGH; Greg follows it more cleanly and reports the twitch immediately.
performance.relationship: Argument sharpens the experiment rather than derailing it.

screenplay: Hessa begins with a boring draw-only check after physical training.
She reframes STOP as ENOUGH: stop feeding, do not freeze.
Greg shapes toward the far mark.
On ENOUGH the region softens toward underlying draw.
His wrist twitches; Hessa orders release.
They call the result different and useful, not clean.

dramatic.state_in: Holl suspects a tester may be too loose; Greg is invited to observe.
dramatic.required_result: Reveal that tester behavior, bench effects, and expert recheck time are entangled.
dramatic.state_out: Greg resists overbuilding the experiment and recommends a smaller decision-focused next test.
dramatic.ownership: Holl owns the decision and cost; testers own local process; Greg owns analysis only when asked.

performance.pressure: Greg loves measurement enough to over-instrument it.
performance.behavior: Holl makes him watch first; Iris reveals a sticky tray; Greg catches the urge to add endless columns and asks what decision Holl needs now.
performance.relationship: Holl can use Greg's mind without surrendering the decision to it.

screenplay: Greg is placed in the testing room with a slate and told to watch.
Two testers process the same lot, then swap benches; apparent tester differences partially move with the bench.
Holl samples clear calls and the simple 'Iris too loose' story weakens.
Iris mentions the right tray sticks. The frame expands.
Greg mentally adds variables until he recognizes the measurement trap.
He asks what decision is needed now and recommends limited bench tracking.

audit.rhythm: EDIT: two lists are already-formed analytical objects

candidates.source: Same lot. Split pieces. Track ambiguity. Sample clear calls. Measure throughput. Measure Holl time.
candidates.replacement: Same lot: split pieces, track ambiguity, sample clear calls, measure throughput, measure Holl time.

candidates.source: More columns. Bench. Reference tile. Tray condition. Dust. Wedge. Piece orientation. Time of day. Moon phase if sufficiently desperate.
candidates.replacement: More columns: bench, reference tile, tray condition, dust, wedge, piece orientation, time of day, moon phase if sufficiently desperate.

dramatic.state_in: Greg is mobile on crutches and learning not to turn ordinary life into a project.
dramatic.required_result: Let a mundane outing with Lyssa demonstrate companionship, adaptive navigation, and tolerance for uncertainty.
dramatic.state_out: Greg chooses simply to stay with Lyssa rather than optimize the hour.
dramatic.ownership: Lyssa owns her work and pace; Greg owns his route; neither turns the other into a project.

performance.pressure: The scene must stay ordinary rather than become a disability lesson or magic debrief.
performance.behavior: Lyssa corrects route mistakes without ceremony, asks about Hessa naturally, and holds Greg's hand without examining it.

screenplay: Lyssa catches Greg over-inspecting pears and steals the best one.
They walk north for her delivery and adjust around street geometry without speeches.
At a dry fountain they watch a child fail with a hoop.
Lyssa asks about Hessa; Greg says a thread moved but may not have been him.
She holds his hand as a hand, not evidence.
With an hour unclaimed, Greg chooses to stay.

audit.rhythm: SOURCE_WIN: short internal corrections are character/comic behavior

dramatic.state_in: Greg is becoming a theatre regular and still wants problems to become engineering tasks.
dramatic.required_result: Show theatre choosing sufficient illusion and continuity over technical perfection.
dramatic.state_out: Greg watches his better repair become unnecessary because the scene already works.
dramatic.ownership: Theatre owns stage utility; Greg owns repair quality only if repair is still needed.

performance.pressure: Greg's instinct is to perfect the hoof board.
performance.behavior: The company keeps rehearsal moving with replacement sounds and temporary cord; Greg builds a better peg, then watches the scene work without it.
performance.relationship: Theatre teaches by refusing to stop for his preferred problem.

screenplay: A servant actor makes a terrible horse noise because the hoof board is missing.
A damaged board plus gray cloth creates an obviously fake but legible horse.
The board breaks; nobody stops the scene.
Crew substitutes box slaps and mouth clicks while timing carries the illusion.
Greg makes a proper replacement peg.
By the time he returns, the spare cup is tied on with cord. Worker: we have horse.

audit.rhythm: SOURCE_WIN: rehearsal repetitions/object beats are timed

dramatic.state_in: One-thread external result was ambiguous but internally useful.
dramatic.required_result: Use a second thread to compare local movement with room noise while preserving safe shaping behavior.
dramatic.state_out: One differential observation improves interpretability but still cannot attribute motion to mana.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns apparatus interpretation; Greg owns hypothesis generation but not conclusion.

performance.pressure: Greg sees a control and wants it to become proof.
performance.behavior: Hessa demonstrates confounds before the attempt; Greg follows the sequence and does not chase movement.
performance.relationship: Hessa permits Greg's technical intelligence inside evidence boundaries.

screenplay: Two threads hang from one frame; Hessa deliberately creates air and vibration to show baseline differences.
Greg recognizes the second thread as a control.
During REACH the near thread moves toward his arm while the far thread does not at that moment.
Greg RETURNs cleanly instead of chasing it.
After release Hessa demonstrates other independent movement.
The useful result is improved comparison, not proof Greg moved the thread.
